title: OpenPLC Editor Desktop
subtitle: Electron desktop application — IEC 61131-3 PLC editor
advisorySource: GitHub Advisory Database via npm audit (equivalent to Dependabot)
headline: Of 143 raw advisories reported against the dependency tree, 3 warrant remediation — all lower-risk denial-of-service items exposed only through an optional live-debug feature — and none are critical or exploitable in normal use. 37 are reachable but constrained by existing controls (a hardened Electron configuration and default-configured DOMPurify); the remaining 103 are not applicable. All three critical-severity advisories are in build/test tooling that is never shipped in the packaged application.
scope: The OpenPLC Editor desktop application is an Electron app: a Chromium renderer process running the React UI and a Node.js main process handling files, packaging, updates, and a language server. It is packaged with electron-builder (asar), and the Electron runtime (Chromium + Node) is bundled into the shipped application. The threat model includes a user opening a malicious project file and an optional live-debug connection to a user-configured PLC runtime.
scopeNote: This SBOM covers the Node.js/npm dependency graph. The build additionally downloads a pinned native strucpp transpiler binary (see binary-versions.json); that binary is tracked separately and is outside the npm SBOM. The bundled Electron runtime (Chromium) is assessed under Mitigated Findings.
methodologyNote: Advisory data was obtained from the GitHub Advisory Database via npm audit (equivalent to GitHub Dependabot alerts). The application is packaged with electron-builder, which prunes development dependencies; only code imported by src (webpack-bundled into dist) plus a minimal runtime module set is shipped in the asar. The bundled Electron runtime is in scope. Reachability was analyzed across both the Electron main (Node) and renderer (Chromium) processes.
licenseNote: No strong copyleft (GPL/AGPL) license is present on the product runtime path. A couple of components declare a custom "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE" field and were reviewed as permissive/first-party. Dual-licensed components (e.g. MPL-2.0 dual with Apache-2.0) are consumed under their permissive option.

affected.rationale: Parsed in the main process only when the user opens a live-debug WebSocket connection to a user-configured PLC runtime (with rejectUnauthorized:false). A malicious/MITM runtime could send forged frames causing memory-exhaustion DoS. Not reachable in normal editing; impact is DoS, not code execution.

mitigated.control: The application ships a hardened Electron configuration: sandbox: true on all windows, with contextIsolation, nodeIntegration:false, and webSecurity at their secure Electron-35 defaults; the preload uses contextBridge; and in production the app loads only local file:// content. These conditions neutralize the high-severity CVE class, which requires rendering hostile web content. Recommendation: update Electron, tighten the CSP (default-src 'none', drop 'unsafe-inline'), add a will-navigate guard.

Called with the default configuration (no RETURN_DOM/ADD_TAGS/SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES), over app-generated markup (search highlights) — the exact intended mitigation. Recommendation: keep dompurify ≥ 3.4.12.

notAffected.components: tar (11, incl. 1 Critical), node-forge (7), webpack-dev-server (4), shell-quote (1 Critical), websocket-driver (1 Critical), immutable (3), svgo, playwright, @babel/*
notAffected.basis: Build, packaging, lint, and test tooling (webpack/electron-builder/sass/babel/playwright). electron-builder prunes development dependencies; these are not in the shipped asar. All three critical advisories fall here.

notAffected.components: axios (28; a dead dependency — not imported anywhere), fast-xml-parser/fast-xml-builder (only the parser is used, the advisory is in the builder), lodash (only safe helpers), js-yaml/yaml (no YAML parsing), uuid (v4 only), qs, serialize-javascript, glob
notAffected.basis: The package (or the specific vulnerable function) is present but never executed with attacker-controlled input.

notAffected.components: form-data, follow-redirects (via unused axios / build publish), minimatch/picomatch, elliptic, path-to-regexp
notAffected.basis: Node/build-only code paths not exercised with adversary input in the running application.

criticalNote: All three critical advisories (shell-quote, tar, websocket-driver) are in development/build/packaging tooling and are pruned from the shipped application. None is present in the delivered product.
remediation: P2: bump socket.io-client so ws ≥ 8.21.0 and socket.io-parser ≥ 4.2.6 (removes the debug-WebSocket DoS surface).
Defense-in-depth: update Electron to a current release; keep dompurify ≥ 3.4.12; tighten the renderer CSP and add a navigation guard; validate schemes before shell.openExternal.

Hygiene: remove the unused axios dependency; configure electron-updater with a fixed signed feed before enabling auto-update; track the downloaded strucpp binary under a dedicated (non-npm) supply-chain inventory.

practices.practice: Deterministic builds from a committed lockfile (npm ci)
Hardened Electron config (sandbox, context isolation, local-only content)
devDependencies pruned from the packaged application (electron-builder)
Automated dependency updates (Dependabot / GitHub Advisory Database)
SBOM generated per release in CycloneDX and SPDX
Keep bundled Electron/Chromium current; tighten CSP; signed auto-update feed
